analysis:
All three changes are documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md, model-registry.md, prefix-cache.md). No code, endpoint, auth, or deployment changes. They describe an unregistered, unpublished Nemotron Super local text path: a recurrent checkpoint bank with chunk-aligned capture (prefix-cache.md head ~295-306), and a media-advertising guard (model-registry.md head 17-22). Relevant threats: T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle, resident tiers); TB-007 (inference engine); T-027/T-012 (model identity and weights).

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- The new Super prefix-cache bank is the resident, opt-in recurrent tier (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1). It stays scoped by authenticated cacheSalt and is not the SSD tier. The text states no SSD or at-rest change, so T-041's at-rest mitigations are unchanged. It does broaden the set of models that can hold resident cross-request KV state. Any future code must preserve cacheSalt scoping and the load-hash and identity bindings.
- The claims in inference.md (media, tools, schemas and client prompt-cache keys rejected; no HTTP route; not registered) are documentation assertions that the supplied evidence does not verify against code. Source for NemotronSuperLocalBinding and ModelMediaPolicy was not supplied; this is a coverage limit, not a finding.
- model-registry.md says staged nemotron_h_omni checkpoints do not advertise media. That is a fail-closed guard, so it is consistent with the threat model.
- The inference.md excerpt shown (lines 1210-1352) is mostly unchanged context. The patch also adds roughly lines 25-171 (truncated), which I could only partly review.

No threat-model update is strictly needed; the existing T-041 resident-tier language could note the Super owner if code enables it.
